web.title: What Is Jev? A Guide to TypeSafe AI's System One Model - LangChain
web.description:
# Building a Harness with Jev
### All about Jev
Jev is actually not a traditional LLM, it doesn’t generate text.

## How to Use Jev with LangChain
```python

from langchain_typesafe import Noul, TypeSafeClassifier

classifier = TypeSafeClassifier()

response = classifier.invoke(
    state=(
        "The deploy failed twice and customers are seeing 500s. "
        "Can someone look now?"
    ),
    questions={
        "urgent": Noul(
            instructions="Does this need attention right now?"
        ),
    },
)

urgency = response.nouls["urgent"].noul
```

## Use Cases
### **Model routing**
```python

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_typesafe.experimental.middleware import (
    ModelChoice,
    ModelRouterMiddleware,
)

router = ModelRouterMiddleware(
    choices={
        "fast": ModelChoice(
            model="openai:luna",
            criteria="Direct lookups, extraction, and localized changes.",
        ),
        "powerful": ModelChoice(
            model="openai:sol",
            criteria="Architecture and high-stakes decisions.",
        ),
    },
    instructions="Choose the least costly model that can complete the task.",
)

agent = create_agent("openai:gpt-5.6-luna", middleware=[router])
```

### **Auto Mode**
```python

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain_typesafe.experimental.middleware import (
    AutoModeMiddleware,
)

guardrail = AutoModeMiddleware(tools=["bash"])

agent = create_agent("openai:gpt-5.6-luna", middleware=[guardrail])
```

web.title: The NEW Blazing Fast AI Model: Jev - YouTube
web.description:
# The NEW Blazing Fast AI Model: Jev
It's not a replacement for the normal LLMs more of a complementary model right.

it's really a game changer, if your process/answer relay only on a combination of call tools only, we dont need an LLM in the loop, just Jev, and more cheaper

One day, you might only want an LLM for the 'human language' stuff - variable/object names, comments, and documentation.

It works as a LLM in the prefill phase, the difference is in the decode phase, it doesn't need to predict the next token because the output is fixed, that is why it's fast.

reminds me of 1B LLM that great at tool calling.

This honestly just seems like a small LLM that is in structured output mode with a temperature of 0.

Weren't first majorly hyped LLMs without thinking like GPT 3.5 also System 1 type?

It's useful for llm as a judge...

I'm not sure about the whole "no LLM is involved" claim -- 90% of the stack sounds like a standard transformer based LLM with parallel encoding but without the autoregression. Essentially it sounds like an RL trained tail-less LLM classifier where the 'next token' are your keywords and probabilities and you read the internal confidence.

So it is classifier model which we had for years but the interesting thing is that is universal like LLM?

Vs LLMs that's huge.

This might be the most exciting AI development so far ... who cares about yet another LLM, you can do so much new stuff with a blazingly fast classifier!

Computer use, but its not an LLM?

This is also where you could bring in an LLM to make more sense of the request to pass back to jev.

Hopefully Jev can be used to enhance LLMs in the future.

Like MTP, i think JEV will be folded inside of LLMs

LLM does exactly the same, no?

LLMs can do structured output but it is not always reliable.

Jev is completely useless spitting out this crap, the same as any other LLM if it isn't useful.

All this video is, is literally "things you can use small LLMs for and by the way Jev can be used for LLM-like tasks"

This flips the mental model of directly asking an LLM for an answer to instead first find reliable sources for the user's prompt, then ask jev for a confidence score based on your question and the provided references.

is it the cerebellum and the basal ganglia for LLMs?
